title: Before the Merge — Data Impact Graph
source: executed SQLite ETL + official OpenLineage SDK + native Relate + real Playwright browser
source_data: fictional sample lots; no customer data
browser_assertions: Playwright screenshots of the real local app, live Relate API

music.source: original procedural composition; no external samples

scenes.name: hook
scenes.voice: A developer proposes changing one lab field from a percentage to a fraction. Before merging, there's one question: what else depends on it?

scenes.name: sql
scenes.voice: We begin with an actual local SQL pipeline. It executes normalization, dry mass, settlements, and carbon intensity. These aren't invented connections on a diagram.

scenes.name: sdk
scenes.voice: The official OpenLineage client emits job and column lineage from those executed SQL expressions. These events identify precisely which input fields feed each output.

scenes.name: import
scenes.voice: One import command turns those events into a persistent embedded Relate graph. No graph server, hosted account, or database credentials.

scenes.name: question
scenes.voice: Now imagine reviewing that proposed moisture change. Search for the original column and ask Relate for its actual downstream paths.

scenes.name: finance
scenes.voice: The first branch reaches supplier payouts, through normalized moisture and dry mass. It's an explicit, inspectable path, not an AI guess.

scenes.name: climate
scenes.voice: The same calculation also reaches carbon intensity. Two business consequences, discovered while the engineer can still change the plan.

scenes.name: precision
scenes.voice: Try field I D instead. That column leads toward field yield, not these finance or climate outputs. Missing lineage is still unknown, not a safety guarantee.

scenes.name: review
scenes.voice: And the engineer can export a real Markdown impact receipt, showing downstream fields and every documented reason. Share it with reviewers before the merge.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.voice: Bring the lineage you already have. Relate makes it locally queryable. Data Impact Graph makes the consequences reviewable, before you change the data.
